subject: Private VPC: networking & allowlist details
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Deployment options — Redwood Private VPC follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciate the walkthrough of FinTechCo's use case and regulatory constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: customer data cannot leave FinTechCo-controlled network; must run in a VPC or on-premise with strict controls.
- Desired features: model access for text generation and embeddings, predictable throughput for peak timeout windows, audit logs and KMS integration.
- Key networking ask: support for PrivateLink or VPC peering and explicit IP allowlist for outbound traffic.

Redwood deployment options based on the call: 
1) Hosted API — not appropriate given data residency/egress constraints.
2) Dedicated capacity — possible if we can guarantee private connectivity and isolation; still runs in Redwood-managed VPCs, so requires an approved connectivity pattern (PrivateLink / peering) and contractual controls.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — recommended for strictest isolation. With Private, we provide a customer-controlled VPC deployment (VPC endpoints, optional on-prem bundle), KMS integration, and audit logs.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
- I’ll send our Private VPC networking checklist and a simple diagram for your infra team to review (network ranges, allowed ports, NAT expectations).
- Marissa (solutions) will follow up with technical details on PrivateLink vs peering tradeoffs and the minimal firewall/allowlist we need.
- Can you confirm FinTechCo’s network contact and preferred cadence for a short technical sync?

Proposed times for a technical sync: Tue/Thu next week 10–11am PT or 2–3pm PT.

Thanks — want to make the path to a Private deployment as frictionless as possible.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Alex / Priya — thanks, and thanks for the diagram. Quick answers inline: 

- PrivateLink vs VPC peering: we support both. PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) is our recommended pattern for least blast radius and simpler routing — we expose a service endpoint and you create an interface endpoint. VPC peering is supported as a fallback for clients with transit gateway constraints but comes with more routing management on your side.

- Allowlisted outbound IPs: For Private deployments we can provide a stable set of NAT egress IPs for your firewall to allowlist. We'll include the exact CIDRs in the checklist. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed hosts) we can also provide static egress IPs when configured.

- KMS integration: yes. Private deployments can integrate with your KMS (bring-your-own-key). Key rotation is supported; we'll provide procedures and an audit log export for compliance.

Next steps (action items):
- I attached the Redwood Private VPC checklist with the required security groups, ports (TLS 443 inbound for control plane, ephemeral ranges for streaming if you choose to allow that), and egress expectations.
- Marissa: can you add the recommended CIDRs we will use for egress and any timing for provisioning PrivateLink endpoints?
- Priya / Alex: confirm a 30-minute technical sync on Thu 11/19 at 10am PT and share any additional compliance docs we should prepare.

Thanks — attaching checklist now.

Best,
Sean

Hi Alex / Priya / Sean,

Quick technical notes from the solutions side — I’ll join the sync and bring a short checklist for each connectivity pattern: 

PrivateLink (recommended):
- You provision an interface endpoint in your VPC. We provide the service name and region.
- Ports: HTTPS (443) only. We terminate TLS at our side by default; mutual TLS is available if required.
- Egress: If you want outbound requests from Redwood to FinTechCo (webhooks, callbacks), we can negotiate IP ranges but most flows are inbound to your PrivateLink.
- Provisioning timeline: usually <48 hours once we have approval and your endpoint created.

VPC peering (fallback):
- Works for customers that need peering/wire-level connectivity. Requires route table updates and potential transit gateway configuration.
- Ports: HTTPS (443) + ephemeral if you enable streaming; otherwise stick to 443.
- We will provide static egress IPs (CIDRs) for allowlisting.

Firewall / allowlist specifics:
- Minimal egress to Redwood: 1-3 static IPs (we'll provide exactly 3 /32s for your firewall).
- Control plane: HTTPS 443 to our control plane during provisioning (these are predictable and will be included in the checklist).

Attachments: I’ve included the network CIDRs we typically allocate for Private deployments and a sample security group template in the checklist.

Looking forward to the sync — Thu 11/19 10am PT works from our side.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
